title: "Online, Reachability-Aware, Sampling-Based Motion Planning"
author: Anonymous Authors
---

## Overview

This work combines the rigorous safety guarantees of **reachable-set analysis** with the flexibility of **sampling-based Model Predictive Control** (MPC) planning. 
By leveraging modern reachability techniques and computation platforms, we compute guaranteed over-approximations of system trajectories under disturbances at runtime, without the need for any expensive pre-computation. 
These over-approximations allow the planner to choose sampled control signals that are **robust to any disturbance realization**, rather than considering only nominal state predictions.
In a simulated study of a dynamic bicycle model, our technique reduces safety violations by over 99%. 
On a real, 1/28th scale model racecar, the vehicle successfully completes **dozens of laps without any crashes**.

## Method Summary

In each control loop, our planner 

1. Samples a large number $N$ of control signals with finite duration $T$ around a reference
2. Integrates an **embedding system** for each signal, giving interval-valued trajectories guaranteed to contain the state of the original system under any (bounded) disturbance signal 
3. Identifies the set of sampled controls that are **provably safe** (i.e. whose interval trajectories do not intersect the unsafe set)
4. Chooses a minimum-cost sampled control from the safe set

By leveraging reachable-set analysis, our controller makes a **provable, deterministic safety guarantee** about signals in its safe set, avoiding stochastic or incentive-driven approaches to choose safe controls. 
Furthermore, our interval-based reachability is fast enough to perform all calculations **fully online** while **scaling to high-dimensional state spaces**.
